source: The Diocesan Cycle of Prayer for the People and Clergy of 2026
sourceFile: "2026DiocesanCycleOfPrayer_2026May_UPDATED.pdf", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 1eZJGIuXP4zeYXWHMsm9vjV7pUwIBarHI, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer").
notes: Genuinely different shape from every other file in this corpus: a full calendar-year 2026 DAILY cycle (365 entries), not weekly -- each day names either a specific congregation, a diocesan ministry/committee, an observance day, or (most days) a dense list of clergy under "The Rev(s):" being commemorated on their ordination/consecration/diaconate anniversary, per the source's own stated purpose (see its Preface). This dense, compound, inconsistent mix does not cleanly split into parish-vs-category the way every other diocese's weekly file does.

Working decision, per this session's own reasoning: each day is recorded as ONE  subject whose  is the source's own day-text verbatim (not attempting to auto-split a parish name out from a clergy-name list, which risks mis-parsing at this density) -- built by a Node parsing script driven from the source's own rendered text, not hand-listed, then spot-checked against the source at the known-tricky dates before being trusted (see below). This means a day naming BOTH a parish and its clergy (e.g. "Calvary Church in Flemington / The Rev James N. Wilson, II", January 1) is one combined subject, not split into separate parish/category subjects the way a weekly diocese file would.

Eight recognized liturgical observance days (Ash Wednesday, Palm/Passion Sunday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Holy Saturday, Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day) get that entry's  set, per this corpus's existing convention (see e.g. episcopal-alabama-2026.json). On a day naming ONLY the observance with nothing else printed (Palm/Passion Sunday, Good Friday, Holy Saturday, Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day), the observance name is also kept as the sole subject's , since entryShape requires a non-empty subjects array and the source genuinely prints nothing else that day; on the two days that pair an observance with a named cleric (Ash Wednesday + The Rev. Canon Bruce W. Woodcock, February 18; Maundy Thursday + The Rev. Andrew C. Hamersley, April 2), the observance name is stripped out of the subject (it already lives in ) and only the cleric's name remains as the subject.

April has no standalone "21" line in the source's own raw text -- day 21's content ("Church of the Resurrection in Millville") sits unlabeled between the "20 Clergy in Transition" line and the "22 Members and Ministry of the Environmental Commission" line. Confirmed positionally (it is day 21, not a continuation of day 20's content) against the surrounding sequential day numbers, and against the source's own PDF page layout -- treated as day 21's own entry here, not folded into day 20.

June 21's source text runs "21Rev. Todd Foster" with no space between the day number and the name (a PDF text-extraction spacing artifact) -- read as day 21, "Rev. Todd Foster", the same way every other day boundary in this file is read, not a separate/different day.

Two spelling variants of an apostrophe (straight ' and curly ’, plus one instance of the reversed curly opening-quote ‘ in "St. Mary‘s Church", August 15) appear inconsistently across the source's own text -- each preserved exactly as the source prints it at that specific point, not normalized to one style throughout, per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a source document.

Built via a Node.js parsing script (not hand-transcribed line by line) against the source's own already-extracted text: day boundaries were found by scanning for a strictly-ascending sequence of 1-2 digit numbers (1, 2, 3, ... N) rather than any bare digit match, specifically to avoid false splits on unrelated numbers embedded in that day's own content (committee ordinal names like "242nd Diocesan Convention"/"243rd Diocesan Convention", November 20-21, were confirmed NOT to cause a false split). Output was spot-checked against the original source text at every structurally ambiguous date named in these notes, plus a normal sample across multiple months, before being trusted; the full parsed set was not individually eyeballed entry-by-entry beyond that.
